items.prompt: Is kicking a ball a push or a pull?

options.why: A pull brings something towards you. A kick sends the ball away.
A kick makes the ball move, so it is a force.

hints: A push moves something away from you.
Where does the ball go when you kick it?
Picture your foot hitting the ball. Does the ball move away or come closer?
items.explanation: Kicking is a push. Your foot pushes the ball away from you.

items.prompt: Is it a push or a pull? Sort the cards.
hints: A push moves something away. A pull brings it closer.
Act out each one with your hands.
Start with the doorbell. Does your finger move away from you?
items.explanation: Pressing a doorbell, throwing a ball and closing a drawer are pushes. Opening a drawer, taking off a sock and picking a mango are pulls.

items.prompt: Dimas opens a drawer to get a pencil. Is it a push or a pull?

options.why: To open a drawer, you move it towards you.
You do not turn a drawer round to open it.

hints: Watch which way the drawer moves.
Does it come towards you or go away?
Act it out: hold a handle and open it.
items.explanation: Opening a drawer is a pull. The drawer moves towards you.

items.prompt: Pushes and pulls are kinds of ___.
hints: There is one science word for pushes and pulls.
This word is used when something is made to move or stop.
It starts with f and has 5 letters.
items.explanation: Pushes and pulls are forces. A force can make things move, stop or change shape.

items.prompt: Which push will make a toy car go further?

figure.alt: A toy car on the floor.

options.why: A small push makes the car go a short way.
Without a push, the car stays still.

hints: Think about pushing gently and pushing hard.
Which push gives the car more speed?
Picture pushing the car very gently. How far does it go?
items.explanation: A bigger push makes the toy car go faster and further.

items.prompt: Choose all the actions that are pulls.

options.why: Kicking moves the ball away from you, so it is a push.

options.text: taking a book off a shelf

options.why: Pressing moves the key down, away from your finger. It is a push.

hints: A pull brings something towards you.
Act out each one.
Start with the curtain. Which way does your hand move?
items.explanation: Opening a curtain, taking a book off a shelf and tugging a rope are pulls. Kicking and pressing are pushes.

items.prompt: Putu is on a swing. How can his friend make it go higher?

options.why: Pulling the swing down would slow it.
Without pushes, the swing slows down and stops.

hints: Think about what makes a swing move.
Does a harder push or a softer push go higher?
Picture pushing a swing gently, then strongly.
items.explanation: A harder push makes the swing go higher and faster.

items.prompt: Kartika squashes a ball of clay flat. What did her push do?

options.why: The clay stays the same colour.
The clay is still there. It is flat now.

hints: Look at the clay before and after.
What is different about it now?
Compare a round ball with a flat pancake.
items.explanation: A push can change the shape of something. Kartika's push changed the round clay into a flat shape.

items.prompt: A ball is rolling towards you. How can you stop it?

options.why: Shouting cannot push the ball.
Looking does not push or pull the ball.

options.text: push against it with your hand

hints: Forces can stop things moving.
Which choice uses a push or a pull?
Picture catching a rolling ball. What do your hands do?
items.explanation: Pushes and pulls can stop moving things. Putting your hand against the ball pushes on it and stops it.

items.prompt: Two teams play tug of war. Which force do both teams use?

options.why: In tug of war, both teams move the rope towards themselves.
The teams do not turn the rope round.

hints: Think about which way each team moves the rope.
Does each team move the rope towards itself or away?
Act it out with a scarf or a towel.
items.explanation: In tug of war, both teams pull the rope towards themselves. The team with the stronger pull wins.

items.prompt: Which one needs a push and a pull?

options.why: Kicking is only a push.

options.text: opening and then closing a door

options.why: Pressing is only a push.

hints: Look for a choice with two actions.
One action moves something towards you and the other moves it away.
Act out opening a door, then closing it.
items.explanation: Opening and closing a door uses a pull one way and a push the other way.

items.prompt: Ravi pushes his toy car the same way each time. He tries a carpet and a smooth floor. Where does it roll further?

figure.alt: A toy car, a rough carpet and a smooth floor.

options.why: The carpet is rough. It slows the car down more.
The rough carpet slows the car more than the smooth floor.

hints: Think about how the two surfaces feel.
Rough surfaces slow moving things down more than smooth ones.
Picture rolling a ball on a rug and on tiles.
items.explanation: The car rolls further on the smooth floor. The rough carpet rubs against the wheels and slows the car down more.

items.prompt: Is closing a drawer a push or a pull?

options.why: You pull to open a drawer, not to close it.
It is one of the two.

hints: Which way does the drawer move?
It goes away from you.
Moving away is a push.
items.explanation: To close a drawer we push it in.

items.prompt: Is throwing a ball a push or a pull?

options.why: The ball goes away from you.
It is a force.

hints: Does the ball come to you?
It moves away.
Moving away is a push.
items.explanation: You push the ball away from your hand.

items.prompt: Is dragging a wagon behind you a push or a pull?

options.why: You do not move it away.
It is a force.

hints: The wagon follows you.
It moves towards you.
Moving towards is a pull.
items.explanation: The wagon comes towards you, so you pull it.

items.prompt: What can a push or a pull do?

options.why: Forces cannot make things alive.
Forces cannot do that.

hints: Think about a ball.
A push makes a ball roll.
It is about moving.
items.explanation: A push or a pull can start something moving. It can also stop it or change its shape.

items.prompt: What happens when you push a toy car harder?

options.why: A bigger push makes it go.
A push stays a push.

hints: A big push is strong.
Try it with a small push first.
It moves more.
items.explanation: A bigger push makes the car go faster and further.

items.prompt: Which one needs the biggest push?

figure.alt: A heavy box, a pencil and a feather.

options.why: A pencil is light.
A feather is very light.

hints: Heavy things need more force.
A feather is light.
Think of moving furniture.
items.explanation: A heavy box needs a big push because it is heavy.

items.prompt: A ball rolls down a slope without a push. What pulls it down?

options.why: The wind did not move it.
There is no magnet.

hints: Things fall down, not up.
Think about dropping a ball.
The Earth pulls things.
items.explanation: The Earth pulls everything down. We call this force gravity.

items.prompt: Is it a push or a pull? Sort the actions.
hints: A push moves things away.
A pull moves things closer.
Start with the rope.
items.explanation: Kicking, closing and pressing are pushes. Zipping open and pulling are pulls.

items.prompt: Choose all the pushes.
hints: A push goes away from you.
You pull a rope towards you.
A drawer comes towards you when you open it.
items.explanation: Kicking, pushing a swing and pressing a bell are pushes. Pulling a rope and opening a drawer are pulls.

items.prompt: Order the pushes from the smallest to the biggest.
hints: A key is very light.
A car is heavy.
The swing is in the middle.
items.explanation: Tapping a key needs a tiny push. A stuck car needs the biggest push.

items.prompt: A push moves things ___ you. A pull moves things ___ you.
hints: Think about pushing a door.
Think about pulling a rope.
The two blanks have different answers.
items.explanation: A push moves things away from you. A pull moves things towards you.

items.prompt: Is it a push or a pull?
head: Action
Push or pull?
hints: Does it come towards you?
Closing sends the door away.
Kick is a push.
items.explanation: Kicking and closing are pushes. Opening a drawer and pulling a rope are pulls.

items.prompt: Ravi plays in the park. He pushes his friend on a swing. Then he pulls a toy cart. At the end he pushes the cart down a slope.

parts.prompt: What does Ravi do to the swing?

hints: Read the second sentence.
Read the third sentence.
The cart is a toy.
items.explanation: Ravi pushes the swing and pulls the toy cart.

items.prompt: Tap the toy you can push so it rolls.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: toy car, book, shoe and cup.

hints: Which one has wheels?
A book does not roll.
It starts with t.
items.explanation: A toy car has wheels. A push makes it roll.

items.prompt: Draw a child pushing a swing. Add an arrow to show the push.

criteria.label: Draws a child and a swing
Draws an arrow in the right direction

hints: The arrow shows which way the swing moves.
Label your arrow.
items.explanation: A push moves the swing away. The arrow points away from the child.

items.prompt: Each child pushes the same box on the same floor. Ana's box moves 5 steps, Ben's 2 steps and Cara's 4 steps. Who pushed hardest?

options.why: His box moved the least.
Ana's box moved further.
The boxes moved different distances.

hints: The box is the same.
A harder push goes further.
Who moved it furthest?
items.explanation: A bigger push makes the box go further. Ana's box went furthest.

items.prompt: A toy car rolls fast on a smooth floor. It slows down on a carpet. What does the carpet do?

options.why: The car gets slower.
The car gets slower.
The car changes speed.

hints: Which gets slower?
A carpet is rough.
Rough things slow other things.
items.explanation: The rough carpet slows the car down. It rubs against the wheels.

items.prompt: You want to move a big heavy box. What is best?

options.text: ask two friends to push too

options.why: One finger is too small.
It will not move by itself.
Blowing is too weak.

hints: Heavy boxes need big forces.
Many people make a bigger push.
Waiting does not work.
items.explanation: More friends push together to give a bigger push.
